<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uintodécimo Kaléndas Ianuárii Luna nona. Anno Dómini 2026
<h>P</h>hilíppis, in Macedónia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Rufi et Zósimi, qui ex illórum número discipulórum fuérunt, per quos primitíva Ecclésia in Iudǽis et Græcis fundáta est; de quorum étiam felíci agóne scribit sanctus Polycárpus in epístola ad Philippénses.
<h>L</h>aodicéæ, in Sýria, pássio sanctórum Theotími et Basiliáni.
<h>I</h>n Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Quincti, Simplícii et aliórum; qui sub Décii et Valeriáni persecutióne passi sunt.
<h>I</h>bídem sancti Moysétis Mártyris.
<h>I</h>tem in Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Victúri, Victóris, Victoríni, Adiutóris, Quarti et aliórum trigínta.
<h>M</h>opsuéstiæ, in Cilícia, sancti Auxéntii Epíscopi, qui, olim sub Licínio miles, pótius elégit cíngulum exúere quam uvas Baccho offérre; factúsque Epíscopus, præclárus méritis quiévit in pace.
<h>T</h>urónis, in Gállia, sancti Gratiáni Epíscopi, qui, a sancto Fabiáno Papa primus eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopus ordinátus est, et multis clarus miráculis obdormívit in Dómino.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.79a1276b56:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 18th 2026, the 9th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the Feast of the Blessed Virgin Mary looking shortly to be delivered.
<h>U</h>pon the same 18th day of December, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Philippi, in Macedonia, (in the year 107,) the holy martyrs Rufus and Zozimus, who were of the number of the disciples by whom the early Church was founded among the Jews and Greeks of whose happy contending holy Polycarp writeth in his Epistle unto the Philippians.
<h>A</h>t Laodicea, in Syria, the holy martyrs Theotimus and Basilian.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Quintus, Simplicius and others, who suffered in the persecution under the Emperors Decius and Valerian.
<h>T</h>here also the holy martyr Moysetes.
<h>L</h>ikewise in Africa also, the holy martyrs Victurus, Victor, Victorinus, Adjutor, Quartus, and thirty others.
<h>A</h>t Mopsuestia, in Cilicia, holy Auxentius, Bishop (of that see;) he was originally a soldier under the Emperor Licinius, but chose rather to cast away his military belt than to offer grapes to Bacchus; he afterwards became a Bishop, and fell asleep in peace, famous for worthy deeds, (fourth century.)
<h>A</h>t Tours, holy Bishop Gratian, who was ordained by holy Pope Fabian as the first Bishop of that city, and fell asleep in the Lord, famous for many miracles. (He was a disciple of the Apostles.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
